text:
Ava (PM): Heads up — we need to lock the GA acceptance checklist for Ship v1 by EOD Fri. Main open items: SLA targets, pricing backstop for burst autoscale, docs plan, and oncall routing. Who's got blockers?

Diego (Eng): SLA: we can commit to 99.9% at per-route level for standard tier but latency SLOs depend on model mix. For heavy LM routes (>=2k tokens) p99 will be higher. Need to decide allowable p99 buckets.

Maya (SRE): Agree. Also need retention window for detailed traces — 7 days is fine for GA, 30 days is a later add-on. Longer retention spikes cost and affects billing.

Jonas (FinOps): Pricing/backstop: pilot customers want predictable billing under burst. Proposal: keep base committed capacity pricing + a capped burst rate with a per-minute cap. We need to articulate the worst-case monthly bill for customers doing 10x burst for an hour.

Ava (PM): Good. Can Jonas draft a short example calc we can paste into the pricing page? Also we should define the fallback policy if Dedicated capacity is exhausted — what model variant do we route to?

Diego (Eng): Fallback: route to quantized variant (q4f16) of the same model with degraded output quality and lower throughput latency. We'll mark it as "compatible fallback" in the routing policy. Need product to approve quality disclaimer.

Priya (Support): Support scope: for GA we can do business-hours SLAs for free accounts and 24/7 for enterprise only. We need clear escalation paths documented — who owns paging for fallback-induced errors? Maya?

Maya (SRE): Yes, SRE owns paging for infra-fallbacks. Support owns customer-facing incidents and first triage. Add runbook: if fallback rate > 5% for 10 minutes, auto-alert oncall and create incident channel.

Ava (PM): Love the runbook idea. Add to docs: in-product banner wording when fallback occurs and a small FAQ for customers. docs-bot, can you create a stub?

docs-bot: created -> ./docs/ga/ship-v1/fallback-notice.md (stub).

Jonas (FinOps): Drafted the example calc: "Example: Customer X has 2 reserved GPUs monthly. Burst to 20 GPUs for 1 hour at peak. Cap policy limits burst charges to 8x baseline hourly rate; worst-case bill for that hour = baseline_hour * 8. We'll translate to tokens & per-request examples." Will commit to pricing page PR.

Diego (Eng): Two implementation asks: (1) need feature flag for routing fallback so we can A/B enable; (2) telemetry metric for fallback_reason with tags {route, model_variant, tenant}. Both small but need eng sprints.

Ava (PM): OK, Diego add estimates. We need the feature flag before pilot cutover.

Diego (Eng): Estimates: flag + config UI ~2 dev-days, metric + dashboard ~3 dev-days, canary rollout pipeline ~1 dev-day. Total ~6 dev-days.

Priya (Support): Docs: include quick triage matrix in the customer-facing doc: "Is it a billing spike? Is it fallback? Is quality changed?" I'll draft. Also recommend adding an in-console "request replay" link for customers to attach failing samples.

Maya (SRE): Monitoring: add 5 min aggregated alert for p95 and p99 latency breaches by route, and an expanded cost alert if burst spend forecast > 120% of committed. That ties into Jonas's backstop.

Ava (PM): Inputs look good. Remaining decisions: precise SLA numbers for latency buckets, final wording for fallback quality disclaimer, and pricing cap math. Can we converge tomorrow morning at 9am?

Jonas (FinOps): I'll post the numeric examples tonight.

Diego (Eng): I'll throw up the feature-flag PR and basic metrics instrumentation branch; mark WIP.

Priya (Support): Drafting triage doc now, will link by morning.

Maya (SRE): I'll add the alert rules to the staging config and add runbook steps.

Ava (PM): Thanks — last ask: add an explicit GA checklist item that docs include an "impact matrix" mapping product tiers -> expected behavior during fallback and billing caps. We can't ship without that.

Priya (Support): noted — I'll own the impact matrix section.

Ava (PM): Great. If no blockers by 9am tomorrow we'll call this locked. :thumbsup:

Diego (Eng): :+1:

Maya (SRE): :thumbsup:

Jonas (FinOps): 👍

Priya (Support): ✅
